q: Which device is installed to prevent ponding in case the primary drain fails in a flat roof system with parapet walls?
n: A secondary (overflow) roof drain or scupper through the parapet carries water off the roof if the primary drain clogs, so water does not pond on a flat roof. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 11 (Storm Drainage – Secondary Roof Drains); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 7.

q: Which drainage system is designed to intercept surface water along a continuous line, often across driveways or in commercial kitchens?
n: A trench (channel) drain is a long, narrow grated channel that intercepts surface water along a continuous line, such as across driveways or in commercial kitchens. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 11; Time-Saver Standards for Site Planning (Surface Drainage).

q: Which device is used to remove accumulated water from a sump pit, typically in basements or low-lying areas?
n: A sump pump lifts water that collects in a sump pit (as in basements or low-lying areas) up to the drainage system. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Sec. 710 (Sumps and Ejectors); Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings.

q: Which drainage component collects surface runoff and sediment before discharging into the storm sewer system, helping to trap debris and prevent clogging of downstream pipes?
n: A catch basin collects surface runoff and lets sediment and debris settle before the water discharges to the storm sewer, which helps prevent clogging downstream. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 11; DPWH Design Guidelines, Criteria and Standards, Vol. 4 (Drainage).

q: Which component provides direct access to a drainage system for clearing blockages without fixture disassembly?
n: A cleanout is an accessible opening with a removable plug in the drainage system. It lets blockages be cleared without taking fixtures apart. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Sec. 707 (Cleanouts).

q: Which component prevents solid debris from entering the drain system at the fixture level?
n: A drain strainer (basket strainer) is the perforated insert at the fixture outlet. It keeps solid debris such as hair and food scraps out of the drain. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Sec. 2 (Definitions – Strainer) and Ch. 4 (Fixture Strainers).

q: Which is the best thinner for acrylic latex?
n: Acrylic latex paints are water-based and thinned with water. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: Which type of paint relies on oil-based thinners, such as turpentine or mineral spirits, to achieve proper consistency while ensuring a durable and long-lasting finish?
n: Alkyd paints are oil-based and thinned with turpentine or mineral spirits. They give a durable finish. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: Which of the following substances is traditionally used to reduce the density and viscosity of oil-based paint, improving its flow and application?
n: Turpentine is the traditional thinner for oil-based paint, lowering viscosity for better flow. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: Which one cannot use water as a thinning material?
n: Enamel (oil- or solvent-based) cannot be thinned with water. Acrylic, emulsion and latex paints can. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: Which component serves as the primary binder in acrylic paint. providing durability, flexibility, color retention. and resistance to w eathering?
n: Acrylic polymer is the binder in acrylic paint. It gives durability, flexibility, color retention and weather resistance. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: What material is applied to smoothen and level interior concrete or CHB walls before painting?
n: A skim coat is a thin cementitious layer that smooths and levels concrete or CHB walls before painting. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: What is the primary purpose of applying concrete primer before painting or coating a concrete surface?
o: To enhance the color of the topcoat
To improve adhesion and seal the surface
To increase the thickness of the concrete
To accelerate the curing of concrete
n: Concrete primer improves adhesion and seals the porous surface, so the topcoat goes on evenly. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: A paint product that serves as an undercoat used to ensure better adhesion of the paint to the surface, increase paint durability and provide additional protection for the surface being painted.
n: A primer is the undercoat that improves adhesion and durability and protects the surface. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: Before applying the final top coat, when painting wood, which material should be used to enhance adhesion, seal the surface, and prevent uneven absorption of paint?
n: For painted wood, a wood primer improves adhesion, seals the surface and evens out absorption before the topcoat. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: When painting bare wood for the first time, which treatment should be applied first to regulate absorption, reduce irregularities and create an ideal base for the paint system?
n: Bare wood to be painted is first given a wood primer. It controls absorption, evens out irregularities and gives the paint system a sound base. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: Which type of paint is best suited for achieving a non-glossy, matte finish on wood surfaces while offering good adhesion and fast drying?
n: Matte acrylic paint gives a non-glossy finish on wood with good adhesion and fast drying. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: A carpenter is restoring antique hardwood furniture and needs a natural resin-based finish that seals the wood, blocks stains and odors, and dries rapidly before subsequent coats are applied. Which material is most appropriate for this application?
n: Shellac is a natural resin finish. It seals wood, blocks stains and odors, and dries very fast between coats. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual; Fine Woodworking finishing references.

q: What is the reason why a concrete neutralizer is needed before painting newly installed concrete walls?
o: For better surface adherence of paint
To prevent the burning of concrete through paint
To counter the alkalinity of new concrete
To seal the porous surface of masonry
n: New concrete is highly alkaline, which attacks paint films. A neutralizer counters that alkalinity before painting. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual (surface preparation of new masonry).

q: You need 4 gallons of paint but the store only sells 1-liter cans. How many cans should you buy?
n: Four gallons = 4 × 3.785 = 15.14 L, so sixteen 1-liter cans are needed. Source: NIST Handbook 44 (1 US gallon = 3.785 L).

q: An architect is specifying a coating system for steel window grilles and metal railings exposed to the outdoors. Which paint type is most appropriate for this application?
n: Enamel paint gives a hard, glossy, weather-resistant film for exterior steel grilles and railings. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: A homeowner is repainting exterior metal railings and window grilles that are fully exposed to sun, rain, and outdoor temperature changes. The new coating must provide a hard, durable, weather-resistant finish that can withstand moisture, UV exposure, and frequent cleaning. The architect advises using a paint type specifically formulated for exterior durability rather than simply choosing a sheen level. Which type of finish is most appropriate for this application?
n: Enamel is a paint type made for hard, durable, weather-resistant finishes on exterior metal. Gloss and semi-gloss are only sheen levels. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: Paint that dries slowly
n: Oil-based paints dry slowly, often taking hours to a day per coat, compared with water-based acrylics. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: Acrytex is a brand of which painting company?
n: Acrytex is a Boysen product line (Pacific Paint (Boysen) Philippines). Source: Boysen product catalog.

q: Best paint finish for a T&B ceiling considering moisture and mildew resistance
n: Semi-gloss resists moisture and mildew and is easy to clean, so it is preferred for toilet-and-bath ceilings. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: A homeowner is selecting a coating for exterior concrete walls that are exposed to sunlight, rain, and normal weathering. The surface is free from major cracks and does not require a crack-bridging coating system. Which paint type is most appropriate for this application?
n: For uncracked exterior concrete exposed to normal weather, acrylic paint is the appropriate weather-resistant choice. Elastomeric is for crack bridging. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: Commonly used paint for concrete interiors of a residential project
n: Latex paint is the usual finish for interior concrete walls in homes. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: Which paint finish is most commonly specified for interior ceilings because it minimizes glare and helps conceal minor surface imperfections?
n: Matte (flat) finish is standard for ceilings. It minimizes glare and hides surface imperfections. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: A three-storey concrete building experiences recurring hairline cracks on its exterior walls due to thermal expansion and contraction. The owner wants a coating that can stretch and bridge these cracks while preventing rainwater penetration. Which characteristic makes elastomeric paint particularly suitable for this application?
n: Elastomeric paint stretches and recovers, bridging hairline cracks as the wall expands and contracts, and keeps rain out. Source: ASTM D6904; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: A durable and flexible paint primarily for exterior walls applied in very thick films
n: Elastomeric paint is a flexible, durable exterior coating applied in very thick films. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: For use on the exterior of a residential project
n: Acrylic paint is the usual weather-resistant exterior finish for residential walls. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: From among the choices, which paint finish is most suitable for general exterior wall applications due to its balance of durability, subtle sheen, and ability to hide surface imperfections?
n: Satin balances durability, a soft sheen and hiding of imperfections, which suits general exterior walls. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: Which paint color reflects the most solar radiation, helping to reduce surface heat gain and improve thermal comfort in buildings?
n: White paint reflects the most solar radiation (highest solar reflectance), lowering surface heat gain. Source: ASHRAE Fundamentals, Ch. 18 (solar absorptance); Cool Roof Rating Council.

q: Paint with a glass-like finish usually used for cornices and moldings
n: High-gloss paint, with a glass-like finish, is typically used on cornices, moldings and trim. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: Which paint will you specify for baseboards and other trims?
n: Enamel is specified for baseboards and trim because it forms a hard, washable film. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: Paint that looks flat and can hide wall imperfections
n: Matte (flat) paint has no shine and hides wall imperfections. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: Paint finish for high-traffic areas
n: Semi-gloss is the durable, scrubbable sheen recommended for high-traffic areas. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: An architect is specifying the wall finish for a school corridor that must withstand repeated scrubbing and allow easy removal of dirt, fingerprints, and scuff marks. Which paint finish should be recommended?
n: Semi-gloss stands up to repeated scrubbing and lets dirt and scuffs wipe off easily, so it suits school corridors. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: Which glossy paint refers to a quick dry solvent that contains resin used primarily in furniture?
n: Lacquer is a quick-drying, solvent-based resin finish used mainly on furniture. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: Which decorative paint finish creates a textured surface that resembles traditional plaster, masonry, or stone, and is commonly used to enhance the appearance of exterior and accent walls?
n: A stucco finish gives a textured surface like traditional plaster, masonry or stone, for exteriors and accent walls. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual; ASTM C926 (portland cement plaster).

q: Which primer best fits the description: a traditional, low-cost, general-purpose rust-preventive primer for steel and iron surfaces that is typically alkyd-based and applied by brush or roller?
n: Red oxide primer is the traditional, low-cost, alkyd-based rust-preventive primer for steel and iron, applied by brush or roller. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual; SSPC Paint 25 (red iron oxide primer).

q: Which paint will you recommend for rooms that require more upkeep, such as kitchens and bathrooms?
n: Enamel forms a hard, washable, moisture-resistant film for kitchens and bathrooms that need frequent cleaning. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: A newly painted exterior concrete wall develops raised bubbles and swollen areas shortly after application. Further investigation reveals that moisture vapor trapped beneath the paint film is forcing the coating away from the substrate. What 'is this paint defect called?
n: Blistering is the raised bubbles that form when trapped moisture vapor pushes the paint film off the surface. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual (paint failures).

q: A painted exterior wall gradually develops a fine, powdery residue on its surface due to prolonged-exposure to sunlight, moisture, and weathering. When touched, the paint leaves a chalk- like powder on 1 the hand. What is this paint defect called?
n: Chalking is the powdery residue left as weathering and UV break down the paint binder. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual (paint failures).

q: A painter applies an excessively thick coat of paint on a vertical concrete wall. Before the coating fully dries, the paint film begins to flow downward, creating uneven drips, curtains, and wavy streams on the surface. What is this paint defect called?
n: Sagging is downward flow (drips, curtains) from paint applied too thick on a vertical surface. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual (paint failures).

q: A painted concrete wall was coated under poor surface preparation conditions, resulting in inadequate adhesion between the paint film and the substrate. Several months later, large sections of the coating begin to detach and come off in sheets and strips, exposing the surface underneath. What is this paint defect called?
n: Peeling is paint coming off in sheets and strips because of poor adhesion from bad surface preparation. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual (paint failures).

q: A crystalline deposit of salt, usually white or grayish tint, that can form on the surface of concrete or masonry when water soluble salts are present in the material, comes to the surface and is left upon evaporation.
n: Efflorescence is the white or grayish salt deposit left when soluble salts migrate to a masonry or concrete surface and the water evaporates. Source: PCA, Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (paints and coatings); PDCA Architectural Painting Specification Manual.

q: Size of G-3/8 gravel
n: G-3/8 gravel is the 3/8-inch nominal size, about 6–10 mm. Source: ASTM C33 (size number 8, 9.5 mm nominal maximum).

q: Size of G-3/4 gravel
n: G-3/4 gravel is the 3/4-inch nominal size, about 10–20 mm. Source: ASTM C33 (size number 67, 19 mm nominal maximum).

q: Different types of sand serve specialized roles in construction, ranging from general filling to structural reinforcement. While some sands focus on stability, others are processed to achieve fine texture and high density, making them ideal for plastering, levelling and masonry applications. Which type of sand undergoes a screening process to ensure consistency in grain size and improved workability for finishing tasks?
n: Vibrasand is a screened (vibro-sieved) sand with consistent grain size and good workability for plastering, leveling and masonry finishing. Source: Local aggregate product classification; ASTM C144 (aggregate for masonry mortar).
